In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Commentary on Surah "Ara'ayta" (Surah 107)

It is Meccan.

It is also said that it is Medinan, and it is said that half of it is Meccan and half Medinan: the first part, up to His words ﴿So woe to those who pray﴾, is Meccan, and the remaining part is Medinan. And Allah knows best.

His Exalted saying: ﴿Have you seen the one who denies the Din?﴾ That is: the recompense (al-jaza'). It is also said: the reckoning (al-hisab), as Mujahid said. The meaning is: Have you seen the one who denies the Din, is he mistaken or correct? That is to say, he is mistaken, so do not agree with him and do not follow him.

And His saying: ﴿So that is the one who repulses the orphan﴾. It has been transmitted in a hadith that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever takes an orphan among the Muslims into his own care, Paradise becomes obligatory for him."

And it was recited in the irregular reading (shadhdh) as: "yadu'u al-yatim" (يَدعُ الْيَتِيم), meaning: he abandons showing compassion and mercy toward him.
And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And does not urge the feeding of the needy﴾. It is said: he does not feed (the needy) himself, nor does he command others to do so.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 107, verses 4–5:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So woe to those who pray, who are heedless of their prayer﴾. Qatadah said: "Negligent."

Al-Mughirah narrated from Ibrahim, who said: "Those who waste the time." This is a well-known statement, and it is reported from a group of the Successors (al-Tabi'un). They mentioned that what is meant by heedlessness (sahw) here is delaying the prayer beyond its time.

The third view: the verse was revealed concerning the hypocrites.

As for the meaning of His saying: ﴿who are heedless of their prayer﴾, it means: if they perform it, they do not expect any reward, and if they abandon it, they do not fear any punishment.

Ibn Zayd said: "They are the hypocrites. They pray it, but prayer is not among their concerns."

Al-Walibi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "They are the hypocrites. When they are present, they perform it out of showing off (riya'), and when they are absent, they abandon it."

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: "It is the hypocrite: when he sees people, he prays, and when people do not see him, he does not pray."

It has also been said: "Sahun" means "lahun" (distracted), and the meaning is that they are occupied with other things, away from it.

Al-Sam'ani's commentary on surah 107, verse 6:

And His saying: ﴿Those who make a show of their deeds﴾ — we have already explained it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 107, verse 7:

And His saying: ﴿And they withhold the small kindnesses (al-ma'un)﴾. ʿAli said: it is the zakat (obligatory alms). Mujahid related this from him, and this view is also related from al-Hasan and Ibrahim al-Taymi.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: it is the loan of items (al-ʿariyah), and it was called ma'un because people help one another (yuʿinu baʿduhum baʿdan).

It has been reported in a khabar (report) that it includes water, salt, the axe, the cooking pot, the flint (al-miqdahah), and what is similar to these.

In some reports from ʿAisha, may Allah be pleased with her, that she asked the Prophet (ﷺ): "What is it that it is not permissible to withhold?" He said: "Water, salt, and fire."

In some narrations there is an addition: "And the stone and the bucket."

Abu al-Husayn Ibn Faris related from his father Faris that al-Ma'un is water. He related it from the people of lexicography (ahl al-lughah), and al-Nahhas also mentioned it in his book.

And they recited poetry:

(He spits out the ma'un's small portion, spitting ...)

And they recited poetry on ma'un meaning zakat:

(A people who, upon Islam, have not given their ma'un, and have wasted the tahlil (the praise of God)...)
